title: reAlpha | Reports Third-Quarter 2026 Results | 2026 | reAlpha Investor Relations: Nasdaq AIRE Market Growth | reAlpha
summary: reAlpha reports Q3 2026 results with revenue growth, improved gross margins, lower operating expenses and a narrower net loss.
body_markdown:
**DUBLIN, Ohio, November 17, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE)** – reAlpha Tech Corp. (Nasdaq: AIRE) (the “Company” or “reAlpha”), an AI-powered real estate technology company, today announced financial results and business highlights for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.


**Financial Highlights**


*(All figures are approximate and compared to the third quarter of 2025 unless otherwise stated.)*


- Revenue totaled approximately $1.6 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to approximately $1.4 million in the third quarter of 2025, an increase of approximately 11%.


- Cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash decreased 92% to approximately $0.8 million as of September 30, 2026, compared to approximately $9.3 million as of September 30, 2025, primarily reflecting cash used to fund ongoing operations and acquisition-related expenditures.
- Gross profit increased to approximately $0.9 million, up from approximately $0.7 million in the third quarter of 2025. Gross profit margin increased to 55% from 52% in the third quarter of 2025, primarily reflecting a more favorable service mix, including higher-margin revenue contributions from Prevu, as well as the absence of higher-cost operations associated with GTG Financial.
- Net loss narrowed by approximately 39% to $3.4 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to approximately $5.6 million in the third quarter of 2025.
- Adjusted EBITDA improved to approximately $(1.9) million, compared to approximately $(4.3) million in the third quarter of 2025, representing an improvement of approximately 56%. The improvement was primarily driven by higher gross profit, supported by increased revenue from the Company's homebuying services segment following the acquisitions of Prevu and InstaMortgage, as well as decreased marketing and advertising expenses, including the absence of expenses associated with the Mercurius Media Capital LP (“MMC”) marketing credits, and reduced professional and legal fees. These improvements were partially offset by higher personnel-related expenses associated with the expanded workforce following the acquisitions.
- Total transaction volume increased approximately 74% to $188.8 million for the trailing twelve months ended September 30, 2026, compared to approximately $108.4 million for the trailing twelve months ended September 30, 2025. Total transaction volume represents the aggregate dollar value of real estate brokerage, mortgage brokerage, direct mortgage lending and title transactions facilitated through reAlpha's services on a trailing twelve-month basis.


“The growth strategy and return-driven spending initiatives we’ve implemented continue to emerge in our financial results.Revenue grew by 11% and our net loss narrowed by 39% in the third quarter compared to the prior-year period,” said Thomas Kutzman, Chief Financial Officer of reAlpha. “Expanding our service offerings through the addition of Prevu and InstaMortgage has strengthened our revenue opportunity, while disciplined spending optimization has significantly reduced our operating expenses year-over-year. These results give us a stronger foundation to build on as we prioritize performance and operating efficiency.”


**Business Highlights**


- In Q3 2026, reAlpha completed the acquisition of InstaMortgage, adding multi-state direct lending, in-house underwriting and funding capabilities to reAlpha’s integrated mortgage platform and expanding its mortgage footprint across 38 states and Washington, D.C. InstaMortgage generated approximately $7.3 million in revenue and $5.3 million in gross profit in 2025 and remained profitable through the first six months of 2026. On an unaudited pro forma basis, reAlpha and InstaMortgage generated approximately $11.8 million in combined revenue and $7.7 million in combined gross profit for 2025.
- On November 4, 2026, reAlpha completed a $1.75 million public offering, generating approximately $1.75 million in gross proceeds before deducting placement agent fees and other offering expenses. The Company intends to use the net proceeds for working capital and general corporate purposes, which could include funding operations, supporting growth initiatives, capital expenditures, potential acquisitions, investments in complementary businesses or technologies, or in connection with the settlement of the Company’s litigation or claims.
- In November 2026, reAlpha appointed Russell Sinclair as Head of Product to lead product strategy and management across the Company’s real estate, mortgage and title technology offerings. Mr. Sinclair was the former Chief Product Officer of Prevu and a product leader at Microsoft, StreetEasy (a Zillow Group company), and House IQ.


“Total transaction volume grew 74% to $188.8 million over the trailing twelve months as we added Prevu and InstaMortgage to the platform,” said Mike Logozzo, Chief Executive Officer of reAlpha. “With both acquisitions complete, our focus is bringing real estate, mortgage and title together in one place. We believe that combination, along with buyer rebates where permitted, creates a simpler and more affordable path to homeownership. Our priority is disciplined execution, because that is how we intend to build long-term value.”


**About reAlpha Tech Corp.**


reAlpha Tech Corp. (Nasdaq: AIRE) is an AI-powered real estate technology company that aims to transform the multi-trillion-dollar U.S. real estate services market. reAlpha is developing an end-to-end platform that streamlines real estate transactions through integrated brokerage, mortgage, and title services. With a strategic, acquisition-driven growth model and proprietary AI infrastructure, reAlpha is building a vertically integrated ecosystem designed to deliver a simpler, smarter, and more affordable path to homeownership. For more information, visit[www.realpha.com](https://www.realpha.com/) .

**Non-GAAP Financial Measures**


To supplement our financial information presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP, we believe “Adjusted EBITDA,” a “non-U.S. GAAP financial measure,” as such term is defined under the rules of the SEC, is useful in evaluating our operating performance. We use Adjusted EBITDA to evaluate our ongoing operations and for internal planning and forecasting purposes. We believe that this non-U.S. GAAP financial measure may be helpful to investors because it provides consistency and comparability with past financial performance. However, this non-U.S. GAAP financial measure is presented for supplemental informational purposes only, has limitations as an analytical tool, and should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for financial information presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP. In addition, other companies, including companies in our industry, may calculate a similarly titled non-U.S. GAAP measure differently or may use other measures to evaluate their performance, all of which could reduce the usefulness of this non-U.S. GAAP financial measure as a tool for comparison. A reconciliation is provided below for our non-U.S. GAAP financial measure to the most directly comparable financial measure stated in accordance with U.S. GAAP. Investors are encouraged to review the related U.S. GAAP financial measure and the reconciliation of this non-U.S. GAAP financial measure to its most directly comparable U.S. GAAP financial measure, and not to rely on any single financial measure to evaluate our business.


We use Adjusted EBITDA, a non-U.S. GAAP financial measure, to evaluate our operating performance and facilitate comparisons across periods and with peer companies. We reconcile our Adjusted EBITDA to our net income (loss) adjusted to exclude interest expense, depreciation and amortization, share-based compensation, and other non-cash, non-operating, or non-recurring items that we believe are not indicative of our core business operations. We believe this measure provides useful insight into our ongoing performance; however, it should not be considered a substitute for, or superior to, net income or other financial information prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP.
